description: A doctor suggests that his patient eat oranges and grapefruit to meet his vitamin C and vitamin A requirements. One orange contains 5 units of vitamin C, 3 units of vitamin A, and 5 grams of sugar. One grapefruit contains 7 units of vitamin C, 5 units of vitamin A, and 6 grams of sugar. The patient must get at least 80 units of vitamin C and 70 units of vitamin A. Since the patent prefers oranges, he must eat at least 2 times as many oranges as grapefruit. How many of each should he eat to minimize his sugar intake?

VitaminCPerOrange.definition: Units of vitamin C per orange

VitaminAPerOrange.definition: Units of vitamin A per orange

VitaminCPerGrapefruit.definition: Units of vitamin C per grapefruit

VitaminAPerGrapefruit.definition: Units of vitamin A per grapefruit

MinVitaminC.definition: Minimum required units of vitamin C

MinVitaminA.definition: Minimum required units of vitamin A

MinOrangeToGrapefruitRatio.definition: Minimum ratio of oranges to grapefruits indicating preference

objective.description: "Minimize the total sugar intake from consuming oranges and grapefruits"

constraints.description: number of oranges >= MinOrangeToGrapefruitRatio * (number of grapefruits)

Oranges.definition: Number of oranges the patient eats

Grapefruits.definition: Number of grapefruits the patient eats
